image_spec: Premium rink coaching graphic. White attacks right to left. A white forward is catching a breakout pass near the right-side boards with speed building. The lone gold defenseman is at the offensive blue line facing the puck with room to pivot.
sit: You are the gold defenseman. The white forward is catching a breakout pass and building speed. What is your best read?
opts: Pivot backward early and match their speed with a controlled gap
Hold the blue line flat-footed and reach if the puck is chipped by you
Lunge straight at the puck carrier even though they already have speed
Turn away from the rush and retreat deep into the slot too early
explain: At U13, a forward with momentum can beat a defender who waits flat-footed. Pivoting early lets you match speed, keep the play in front of you, and control the gap.
overlay_intent: Gold arrow showing the defenseman pivoting backward to match speed; red X over the flat-footed step-up lane.
reviewerNote: Removed body-check framing, made the wrong options realistic gap mistakes, and kept the read to one still-frame cue: speed building versus defender gap.

image_spec: Premium top-down rink graphic. White attacks bottom to top. The puck is now with a white defense partner in the neutral zone after a regroup. Two white forwards are curled back and flat-footed. The gold defenseman is backing in with open ice in front.
sit: The puck is back with a white defense partner and their forwards are flat-footed. You are the gold defenseman. What is your read?
opts: Step up under control to tighten the gap and take away open ice
Keep backing in even though the white forwards have no speed
Drift sideways toward the benches and give up the middle lane
Drop to one knee in the neutral zone to block a pass that is not there
explain: When the attack slows down, the defender can take ice back. Stepping up under control closes the gap before the white forwards can rebuild speed.
overlay_intent: Gold arrow showing the defenseman stepping up into the neutral zone; red X over the backward retreat path.
reviewerNote: Changed the motion-dependent pass sequence into a frozen regroup frame and sharpened the retreat decoy.

image_spec: Premium rink coaching graphic. White attacks left to right. A white puck carrier is on the right boards near the top of the gold faceoff circle. The gold defenseman has a tight one-stick-length gap and inside body position.
sit: You are the gold defenseman defending the rush. You have a tight gap at the faceoff dot and inside position. What is the correct read?
opts: Keep your stick on the ice and steer the puck carrier down the boards
Back into the slot and give the puck carrier the middle of the ice
Dive at the puck and hope the carrier cannot step around you
Stop your feet and wait for the puck carrier to choose first
explain: A tight gap at the dot is a chance to finish the angle. Keep skating, protect the middle, and steer the puck carrier toward the lower-danger boards.
overlay_intent: Gold arrow steering the white player down the boards; red X over the path backing off into the slot.
reviewerNote: Removed dangerous dive language from the keyed play, clarified inside position, and made backing into the slot the tempting wrong read.

image_spec: Premium top-down rink graphic. Gold attacks bottom to top. After a dump-in, a white defender has the puck on the right half wall and is looking down while bobbling it. The gold winger is high on the same boards with a clear lane to close.
sit: You are the gold winger. The white defender is bobbling the puck on the boards with their head down. What should you do?
opts: Pinch down under control along the boards to close the gap and trap them
Back out to the neutral zone and give them time to settle the puck
Drift to the middle of the blue line and tap your stick for a pass
Leave the strong side and skate all the way to the far boards
explain: Gap control is not only for defensemen. When an opponent bobbles the puck, close quickly and under control before they recover time and space.
overlay_intent: Gold arrow showing the winger pinching down the boards at the fumbling white player; red X over the retreat path.
reviewerNote: Kept the offensive-zone pinch but made it controlled and age-appropriate rather than purely aggressive.

sit: You are the first gold forechecker. The white defenseman is looking to skate out the right side of the net. What is your angle of approach?
opts: Take an inside-out arc toward the post so your stick removes the middle
Chase in a straight line at their back and let them choose either side
Wait still near the blue line until the puck comes to you
Skate to the white goalie and screen a shot that is not coming
explain: Angling starts by taking away the best ice. An inside-out route cuts the rink in half and steers the puck carrier toward the boards.
overlay_intent: Gold curved arrow from the middle toward the post; red X over the straight-line chase.
reviewerNote: Replaced chase language with role-based first forechecker wording and made the approach visible from one frame.

sit: You are tracking the white puck carrier in the neutral zone. Where should you put your body and stick?
opts: Keep your body inside and your stick in the middle lane to steer them outside
Chase from directly behind and try to lift their stick after they pass you
Skate straight to center ice and face them head-on with no angle
Let them pass you so you can try to block a later shot
explain: If you are behind the rush, you are chasing. Good angling puts your body and stick inside the dangerous lane so the puck carrier is steered to the boards.

sit: You are the gold winger. The white defenseman is walking the blue line toward the dangerous middle. How should you approach?
opts: Approach from the inside slot area and angle them back toward the boards
Attack from the wall side and give them the middle shooting lane
Leave the point player and cover a white center who is already marked
Sink below the hash marks and let the blue line stay open
explain: The middle lane is the dangerous ice. Approach from inside out so the white defenseman is pushed back toward the perimeter.

image_spec: Premium top-down rink graphic. White attacks bottom to top down the left wing. The gold defenseman has a tight inside gap. A gold backchecker is trailing behind the puck carrier with a lane to the inside shoulder.
sit: You are the gold backchecker. Your defenseman has a good inside gap on the white puck carrier. What is your role?
opts: Backcheck toward the inside shoulder to squeeze the puck carrier toward the boards
Skate past the puck carrier and try to take the puck head-on
Coast at the blue line and wait to see who wins the rush
Leave the play and skate to the far side where no threat is located
explain: When the defenseman owns the inside gap, the backchecker should add pressure from behind and inside. That squeezes the puck carrier's space without opening the middle.
overlay_intent: Gold arrow from the backchecker toward the white puck carrier's inside shoulder; red X over the path skating past them.

sit: You are the high gold forward. Your winger is battling two defenders in the corner. Where is your best support position?
opts: Stay high in a quiet slot pocket as a passing option
Dive into the corner and bring another defender into the pile
Drift all the way back to the center red line
Stand below the goal line where your teammate cannot pass to you
explain: When two defenders are already in the corner, joining the pile removes a passing option. Staying high gives the puck carrier a useful outlet if they win possession.

Hug the right boards all the way down and stay easy to ignore
Stop at the blue line and watch the puck carrier attack alone
Trail directly behind the puck carrier in the same left-side lane

Dive into the deep corner and leave the half wall open
Skate across to the weak-side half wall while the puck is on the strong side
Retreat to the center red line before pressure is beaten

Sprint straight in so one cutback can beat you cleanly
Stop at the top of the circles and let the breakout start
Peel away from the play and give the defenseman both sides

Dive deep alone against three white players and hope to steal the puck

Stand still on the center red line and let them attack with speed

Double-team the puck carrier on the boards and leave the middle open
Stop at the blue line and watch the rush enter the zone

Skate to the goal line even though the late trailer is open
Follow the puck carrier into the corner and leave the slot uncovered
Stand directly in front of your goalie and block their view
explain: The late trailer is often the open danger on an odd-man rush. The first forward back must identify that second wave and take away the high-slot option.

sit: You are the gold backchecker. A rebound is loose in the crease and you are looping behind the net. What is your mistake?
opts: You are gliding behind the net instead of stopping hard at the crease to clear the puck
You are watching the shooter after the puck has already rebounded loose
You are waiting for the goalie to cover it while the puck is still free
You are looping toward the corner instead of returning to the dangerous ice
explain: Backchecking continues until the puck is safe. A loose puck in the crease is immediate danger, so stop at the net and help clear it.
